passages.note: Senate Third Reading roll call for HB2721 (2024); Gowan voted Aye.

passages.provision_quote: The municipality may not do any of the following: 1. Discourage the development of middle housing through requirements or actions that individually or cumulatively make impracticable the permitting, siting, or construction of middle housing.
passages.note: Enacted text (Chapter 197) bars municipalities from using zoning/permitting rules to block middle housing and requires they allow it.

rows.reasoning: Gowan voted Aye (GOWAN Y, Passed 21-7-2-0-0 Amended) on HB2721 (2024), which bars municipalities from using zoning and permitting rules that block middle housing and requires they allow it as a permitted use. That supports the direction of 'rely on the market to set prices and supply — at most, cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building,' but one deregulation law limited to middle housing cannot show he wants only that and nothing more, so per the refined preemption rule this is on-question but direction-only, not rung-shaped.
needs_source: Gowan's own statement on his broader housing position (subsidies vs. pure deregulation) to resolve whether rung 4 or rung 5 applies
